body:
This PR tries to implement the fix for #818. However it appears that we only retrieve values up to the most last open item. This means that even we can add the `hasChildren` data, this is incorrect as it will be true only if it's open and it's not a very useful information for the user since they would have already open the item.

[See it live](https://deploy-preview-2638--algolia-instantsearch.netlify.com/v2/dev-novel/?selectedStory=HierarchicalMenu.with%20custom%20item%20template).

> IMHO this proves that it's not really a viable option and therefore we should not add it to the project.

Yep at this point only the API could maybe give us this sort of information (which is very valuable), otherwise we'd have to do up to "number of items of hierarchical menu displayed x requests" to know if any item has any sub elements coming afterwards, which on the frontend is a no-go.

cc @mthuret FYI, limitation of hierarchical facets on the frontend: can't inform the user UX wise if an element has or has not subelements before the user refines it.

title: feat(connectHierarchicalMenu): add hasChildren to items
